Wasp automatically invalidates a Query's cache whenever an Action that declares the *same* Entity runs.                 [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `main.wasp` file defines the complete application structure through declarative configuration:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Configuration Section|Purpose|Generated Output|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`db.seeds`|Database seeding|Development data|\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database - Wasp - ContextQMD\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://contextqmd.com/libraries/wasp/versions/0.22.0/pages/web/versioned_docs/version-0.19/tutorial/05-queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The primary way of working with Entities in Wasp is with Queries and Actions, collectively known as ***Operations* **.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries are used to read an entity, while Actions are used to create, modify, and delete entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Since we want to list the tasks, we'll want to use a Query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To list the tasks, you must:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Create a Query that fetches the tasks from the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Update the `MainPage.{jsx,tsx}` to use that Query and display the results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We need to add a **query** declaration to `main.wasp` so that Wasp knows it exists:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getTasks {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Specifies where the implementation for the query function is.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// The path `@src/queries` resolves to `src/queries.js`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// No need to specify an extension.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { getTasks } from "@src/queries",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Tell Wasp that this query reads from the `Task` entity.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp will\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// automatically update the results of this query when tasks are modified.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { Task } from "wasp/entities";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import type { GetTasks } from "wasp/server/operations";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 6. Modifying Data\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/actions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Let's now learn about Actions so you can add and update tasks in the database.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We must first declare the Action in\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { action, app, page, query, route } from "@wasp.sh/spec"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Prisma Schema File | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-07-15, last updated: 2024-10-15, [Read more](https://wasp-lang.dev/docs/0.14.0/data-model/prisma-file)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp uses Prisma to interact with the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In Wasp, the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`schema.prisma` file is located in your project's root directory:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'`.`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'├── main.wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...Wasp uses the\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`schema.prisma` file to understand your app's data model and generate the necessary code to interact with the database.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`datasource` block defines which database you want to use (PostgreSQL in this case) and some other options.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Finally, Prisma models become Wasp Entities which can be then used in the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`main.wasp` file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`datasource db {`\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Next, let's define how to do something with these data models!\n"[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Query invalidation/updating · Issue #63 · wasp-lang/wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-09-29, last updated: 2025-09-10, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/issues/63)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Implement "entities as resources" solution -> each operation can specify entities it uses and they are automatically used for automatic cache invalidation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'react-query offers way to refetch/invalidate specific query either by referencing it via key or by using methods returned by it when used via useQuery hook.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Via key is currently not a friendly option for Wasper because cache key is not part of public Wasp API (but we could make it part of it, it is there).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Using methods returned by useQuery works for Wasper, but with that we can affect query only if we are next to the place where it is used via useQuery hook, which will often not be true.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'With Wasp:\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Actions | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/actions)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since Wasp uses *react-query* for Query management, we must make sure to invalidate Queries (more specifically, their cached results managed by *react-query*) whenever they become stale.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's possible to invalidate the caches manually through several mechanisms *react-query* provides (e.g., refetch, direct invalidation). However, since manual cache invalidation quickly becomes complex and error-prone, Wasp offers a faster and a more effective solution to get you started: **automatic Entity-based Query cache invalidation**. Because Actions can (and most often do) modify the state while Queries read it, Wasp invalidates a Query's cache whenever an Action that uses the same Entity is executed.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'| | |export const invalidateQueriesUsing = (resources) => {|\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/query-invalidation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For that purpose, the QueryClient has an invalidateQueries method that lets you intelligently mark queries as stale and potentially refetch them too!\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Query Invalidation - Pinia Colada\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-30, [Read more](https://pinia-colada.esm.dev/guide/query-invalidation.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, you can also manually invalidate queries using the Query Cache.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can directly invalidate queries using the query cache.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"This marks matching queries as stale, prompting a refetch if it's active (i.e., currently used by a component).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'You can filter queries by `key`, `status`, `active`, and more.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'exact\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// Refetch all active queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryCache\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'invalidateQueries\n'[39m +

                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, `invalidateQueries()` invalidates all queries (both active and inactive) but only refetches active queries. Inactive queries are marked as stale and will be refetched when they become active again. You can change this behavior by passing a second parameter to refetch all queries:\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# React-Query and Query Invalidation Question\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-09-19, last updated: 2026-05-18, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63968683/react-query-and-query-invalidation-question)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The mutation does not automatically triggers a refetch.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The way to achieve this using react-query is via queryCache.invalidateQueries to invalidate the cache after the mutation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'From the docs:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> The invalidateQueries method can be used to invalidate and refetch single or multiple queries in the cache based on their query keys or any other functionally accessible property/state of the query.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'So you can configure the `useMutation` to invalidate the query when the mutation settles.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- No, actually, `refetch` will force the queries to fetch no matter what, whereas `invalidate` only push fetching when the queries are not being used.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# React Query questions - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-07-30, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1267894500659953716)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- In Wasp, the cache keys are handled internally and are not expected to be supplied by the user.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to access the Query cache key, you can do so by accessing the\n'[39m +

                      [32m'const queryKey = getTasks.queryCacheKey\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"(**source**(https://wasp-lang.dev/docs/data-model/operations/actions#advanced-usage)) As for the issue you're experiencing with the cache keys, it's hard to say without more information.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are several ways to invalidate/update the cache in Wasp, including directly (via the cache key or methods returned by\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Query invalidation/updating · Issue #63 · wasp-lang/wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-09-29, last updated: 2025-09-10, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/issues/63)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'react-query offers way to refetch/invalidate specific query either by referencing it via key or by using methods returned by it when used via useQuery hook.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Via key is currently not a friendly option for Wasper because cache key is not part of public Wasp API (but we could make it part of it, it is there).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are 3 main ways of invalidating/updating cache:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Directly -> action directly invalidates/updates cache of specific query/queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Choosing this specific order of queryKey items allows us to invalidate features for specific project:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [projectId, "features", "list"] });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// used when:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// adding feature\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// updating feature (but only if updating basic info, otherwise it's not required)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// deleting feature\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'But it also extensible to other needs:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [projectId, "features", "details", featureId] }); // invalidate specific feature\n'[39m +
                      [32m'qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [projectId, "features"] }); // invalidate all features related\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryClient\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Query Invalidation | TanStack Query React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-05, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-invalidation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For that purpose, the QueryClient has an invalidateQueries method that lets you intelligently mark queries as stale and potentially refetch them too!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate every query in the cache\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryClient.invalidateQueries()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate every query with a key that starts with `todos`\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a query is invalidated with invalidateQueries, two things happen:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- It is marked as stale.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This stale state overrides any staleTime configurations being used in useQuery or related hooks\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- If the query is currently being rendered via useQuery or related hooks, it will also be refetched in the background\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When using APIs like invalidateQueries and removeQueries (and others that support partial query matching), you can match multiple queries by their prefix, or get really specific and match an exact query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can even invalidate queries with specific variables by passing a more specific query key to the invalidateQueries method:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you find yourself wanting **even more** granularity, you can pass a predicate function to the invalidateQueries method.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function will receive each Query instance from the query cache and allow you to return true or false for whether you want to invalidate that query:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's possible to invalidate the caches manually through several mechanisms *react-query* provides (e.g., refetch, direct invalidation).\n"[39m +
                      [32m'However, since manual cache invalidation quickly becomes complex and error-prone, Wasp offers a faster and a more effective solution to get you started: **automatic Entity-based Query cache invalidation**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Because Actions can (and most often do) modify the state while Queries read it, Wasp invalidates a Query's cache whenever an Action that uses the same Entity is executed.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `updateQuery` required\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The function used to perform the optimistic update.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It should return the desired state of the cache.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `item` - The argument you pass into the decorated Action.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `oldData` - The currently cached value for the Query identified by the specifier.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you decide to use *react-query*'s API directly, you will need access to Query cache key.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp internally uses this key but abstracts it from the programmer.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Still, you can easily obtain it by accessing the `queryCacheKey` property on any Query:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { getTasks } from "wasp/client/operations"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const queryKey = getTasks.queryCacheKey\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Should I manually invalidate the query with React Query's queryClient.invalidateQueries, or is there a more idiomatic way to handle this in Wasp?"[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Query Invalidation | TanStack Query Lit Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-05, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/lit/guides/query-invalidation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use queryClient.invalidateQueries to mark matching queries stale and refetch active observers.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryClient.invalidateQueries()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'queryClient.invalidateQueries({\n'[39m +

                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a query is invalidated:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- It is marked stale, overriding any staleTime\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- If a matching query is active in a controller, it can refetch in the background\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Invalidate queries doesn't work [React-Query] - Stack Overflow\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-07-29, last updated: 2026-03-20, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68577988/invalidate-queries-doesnt-work-react-query)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you used `enabled` option in `useQuery` than such queries are ignored by `invalidateQueries`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'From docs:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/react/guides/disabling-queries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> The query will ignore query client invalidateQueries and refetchQueries calls that would normally result in the query refetching.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# TanStack Query (Formerly React Query): The Basics - Atomic Spin\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-08-21, last updated: 2026-07-03, [Read more](https://spin.atomicobject.com/basics-tanstack-query/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This instance is essential for managing query and mutation data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Query invalidation is the process of marking a query as stale, prompting it to refetch data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'const queryClient = useQueryClient();\n'[39m +

                      [32m'await queryClient.invalidateQueries();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate queries that match a specific query key\n'[39m +
                      [32m"await queryClient.invalidateQueries(['users']);\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Invalidate queries that exactly match a specific query key\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await queryClient.invalidateQueries({\n'[39m +
                      [32m"queryKey: ['users', 1],\n"[39m +
                      [32m'exact: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Properties for Invalidating Queries:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **queryKey**: Specifies which queries to invalidate.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be a partial key (e.g., [‘users’]) or an exact key (e.g., [‘users’, 1]).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note that the first argument to the query key array should be a unique string or identifier to ensure that queries are uniquely identifiable and managed correctly by the query client.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **exact**: If true, only queries with the exact queryKey will be invalidated.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 查询失效 | TanStack Query React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-01, last updated: 2025-05-19, [Read more](https://zh-hans.tanstack.dev/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/query-invalidation)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'单纯等待查询因陈旧而重新获取并不总是有效，特别是当您明确知道由于用户操作导致某查询数据已过期时。为此，QueryClient 提供了 invalidateQueries 方法，允许您智能地将查询标记为陈旧状态，并可能触发重新获取！\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'queryClient.invalidateQueries()\n'[39m +

                      [32m'invalidateQueries API 非常灵活，如果您\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# tanstack query invalidation — typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-05-21, last updated: 2026-08-11, [Read more](https://typescript.nicedx.com/tanstack-query-cache-invalidation/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Calling `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['posts'] })` does not delete anything.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It marks every matching query as stale and triggers a refetch for any query currently mounted by an active observer.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Unmounted queries get marked stale silently and refetch the next time a component subscribes to that key.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'That distinction matters: invalidation is cheap, idempotent, and safe to call from anywhere.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`invalidateQueries({ queryKey: postKeys.all })` matches every key in the tree by prefix.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`invalidateQueries({ queryKey: postKeys.lists() })` invalidates list queries but leaves detail queries alone.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`invalidateQueries` marks data stale and triggers refetch.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`removeQueries` deletes the cache entry entirely.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Reach for `removeQueries` after a sign-out, a tenant switch, or any context change where the previous data should never appear again — even briefly:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Prefer `setQueryData` when the mutation response contains the canonical update.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Fall back to prefix `invalidateQueries` when the server-side derivation is non-trivial.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. Reach for predicate invalidation only when key structure does not capture the affected set.'[39m

Ss   18:36   0:00 bash -lc set -o pipefail; cat > /tmp/pochi_cmd.sh << \'CMD_EOF\' set -o pipefail cat <<\'EOF\' | pochi --model google/gemini-3.5-flash --max-steps 200 --max-retries 10 --blobs-dir /logs/agent/pochi/blobs --experimental-stream-trajectory /logs/agent/pochi/trajectory.jsonl --experimental-stream-trajectory-strip-duplicates > >(tee /logs/agent/pochi/stdout.txt) 2> >(tee /logs/agent/pochi/stderr.txt >&2) # Reactive Project Task Board with Manual React Query Cache Management  ## Background You are working on a Wasp (wasp.sh) full-stack app called **taskboard**. Wasp compiles a declarative `main.wasp` file together with your React/Node code into a full-stack app, using Prisma for the database and React Query for client-side data fetching. Wasp automatically invalidates a Query\'s cache whenever an Action that declares the *same* Entity runs. This automatic, entity-based invalidation is convenient but coarse: it does not understand *derived* or *relational* data, so a computed Query that depends on another entity only through a relation will NOT be refreshed automatically. Your job is to build a small task board that relies on automatic invalidation where it works and falls back to explicit React Query cache management where it does not.  A Wasp project skeleton already exists at the project path. You must implement the data model, the Operations, the database seed, and the page.  ## Requirements - Model two entities in the Prisma schema: a **Project** (has a name and many tasks) and a **Task** (has a title, a done flag, and belongs to a Project). - Implement a Query `getTasks` that returns every task (with its id, title, done state and project id). - Implement a computed/derived Query `getProjectStats` that returns, for every project, an object with the project\'s id, its name, the total number of tasks in that project, and the number of done tasks in that project. - Implement an Action `addTask` that creates a new task in a given project, and an Action `toggleTask` that flips a task\'s done state. - Build a single page (mounted at `/`) that lists every project together with its live statistics, lists all tasks, lets the user add a task to a project, and lets the user toggle a task\'s done state. Every displayed value must update reactively after an Action, WITHOUT a full page reload. - Provide a database seed that populates the initial board (see the hint below for the exact required data).  ## Implementation Hints - Wasp automatically invalidates a Query whenever an Action that shares one of its declared entities runs. Use this for the plain task list, but remember it only fires on exact entity overlap: declare the entity `getTasks` reads so Wasp keeps it fresh automatically. - `getProjectStats` is an intentionally decoupled aggregate: it MUST be declared so that it depends only on the `Project` entity (do NOT add `Task` to its entity list). Because of that, adding or toggling a task will NOT automatically refresh it. You must keep it up to date on the client yourself using React Query\'s cache mechanisms: obtain the `QueryClient` (react-query is bundled with Wasp and importable from `@tanstack/react-query`) and invalidate/refetch the stats Query after the relevant Actions. A Wasp client Query object exposes its cache key via its `queryCacheKey` property, which you can use as the react-query query key. - Compute the derived statistics from the database (e.g. via the Project entity\'s Prisma relation / relation counts); do not maintain a separate hand-rolled counter table. - Use a local SQLite database (the default dev database). Run `wasp db migrate-dev` after changing the schema so it is applied, and commit the generated migration. - Add exactly one Wasp database seed named `devSeed` (declared under the app\'s `db.seeds`). It must be safe to run repeatedly and must always leave the database in exactly this state: a project named `Work` containing two tasks titled `Ship release` (done) and `Write docs` (not done); and a project named `Home` containing one task titled `Buy groceries` (not done). Running it should clear any prior projects/tasks first so the result is deterministic. Your job is to build a small task board that relies on automatic invalidation where it works and falls back to explicit React Query cache management where it does not. Every displayed value must update reactively after an Action, WITHOUT a full page reload. - Provide a database seed that populates the initial board (see the hint below for the exact required data).  ## Implementation Hints - Wasp automatically invalidates a Query whenever an Action that shares one of its declared entities runs. Because of that, adding or toggling a task will NOT automatically refresh it. You must keep it up to date on the client yourself using React Query\'s cache mechanisms: obtain the `QueryClient` (react-query is bundled with Wasp and importable from `@tanstack/react-query`) and invalidate/refetch the stats Query after the relevant Actions. A Wasp client Query object exposes its cache key via its `queryCacheKey` property, which you can use as the react-query query key. - Compute the derived statistics from the database (e.g. via the Project entity\'s Prisma relation / relation counts); do not maintain a separate hand-rolled counter table. - Use a local SQLite database (the default dev database). Running it should clear any prior projects/tasks first so the result is deterministic.             [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
